name: Walkable Environment Audit from Street View (Kaohsiung and Chiayi)
description:
Method replication: participants rate 4 street views from Kaohsiung and Chiayi (Taiwan) on 24 walkability attributes from the paper's instrument (social safety, traffic safety, aesthetics, sidewalk quality, physical barriers, amenities, others), each on the paper's 1–5 scale with its own end labels; the images are not the paper's stimuli (56 Google Street View images of central Kaohsiung and Chiayi, 2020–2026, fetched for this template; the city is shown under each image).
Original study: Chiang, Sullivan & Larsen (2017), "Measuring Neighborhood Walkable Environments: A Comparison of Three Approaches", International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health 14(6), 593. Six neighbourhoods (500 m radius), three relatively good and three relatively poor, in Kaohsiung (higher-quality walking environment) and Chiayi (lower quality) were assessed with 27 attributes on 1–5 scales by 90 participants: local residents of three or more years, trained field visitors, and trained students who browsed every street of each neighbourhood in Google Street View. Agreement between approaches was compared with intraclass correlations.
Differences from the original study: (1) single street views instead of browsing a whole neighbourhood, so the three attributes that need the street network (intersections, alternative paths, cul-de-sacs) are left out; (2) views come from random street points in each city centre, not the paper's six selected neighbourhoods, and are newer (2020–2026 instead of 2014); (3) no training session; (4) a question on whether the participant has lived in either city for three years or more replaces the separate resident, field-visit and Street View groups.
author: Chiang, Sullivan & Larsen
